title: Tamsin and the Letter
premise: In the final winter of the Republic of Vessany, courier Cyrus Yarrow carries a sealed diplomatic letter to the coastal city of Marrowgate, believing himself a mere messenger in a war already lost. When pirates board his ship and the letter's seal breaks, he discovers it names the Aldery family — his own estranged kin — as traitors marked for execution by the republic's collapsing regime. Sheltered by the Alderys, Cyrus must decide whether to deliver the letter and save his career or destroy it and condemn himself. As soldiers close in, he secures passage on a ship leaving on the morning tide — but only one berth remains, forcing him to choose between his grandmother, who raised him, and his young cousin, who carries the family's future. He gives the berth to the child, stays behind with his grandmother, and is arrested at dawn; yet the letter's destruction, witnessed by a sympathetic officer, plants the seed of the resistance that will one day restore the family name.
about_author: Petra Brightwater is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing the private correspondence of displaced families. Her fiction explores how ordinary people become accidental witnesses to history.

chapters.title: The Weight of Sealed Things
chapters.summary: Cyrus Yarrow boards the mail ship Vesperine bound for Marrowgate, carrying a letter whose contents he believes are beneath his notice. Through his eyes we see a man proud of his neutrality, rehearsing his delivery speech while the republic burns behind him. A storm forces an unscheduled stop, and he glimpses refugees on the docks — history happening to other people, elsewhere. The emotional beat is complacency about to crack.

chapters.title: What the Water Gave Back
chapters.summary: Pirates board the becalmed Vesperine at night. In the chaos the letter's wax seal splits, and Cyrus reads the impossible: the Aldery family — his mother's people, whom he has never met — named as traitors with a bounty on their heads. POV shifts between Cyrus and Maren Aldery, the grandmother watching for a courier who may be her grandson. The beat is shock giving way to reluctant recognition.

chapters.title: A House of Borrowed Time
chapters.summary: Cyrus delivers the letter anyway — duty first — then, haunted, seeks out the Aldery house and finds his grandmother Maren and cousin Ilsa living under false names. He hides them from a soldier's sweep, burning half the letter to buy time, and learns the regime executes whole households. Torn between self-preservation and blood, he negotiates with a smuggler for berths on the morning tide. The beat is complicity turning into commitment.

chapters.title: One Berth Before the Tide
chapters.summary: Soldiers surround the harbor quarter at dawn; the smuggler's ship can take only one passenger. Cyrus chooses Ilsa, slipping her the intact half of the letter as proof of innocence for the future. He stays with Maren as the door is broken down, surrendering quietly when she refuses to run. An officer who once doubted the regime lets the letter's ashes stay buried. The beat is grief transmuted into quiet, defiant hope.
